purpose: Show the weight-space-editing result as a figure in the style of the WSP tutorial's table: for the base model and each saved checkpoint, test word error rate with its CI, the paired change versus base, and the downstream sentiment macro-F1 with its CI.
filter: all three rows (base, fp10, fp17); mark fp17 as the registered checkpoint
encodings: three horizontal dot-and-interval panels sharing the row axis (base, fp10, fp17 top to bottom): (1) test WER vs human transcripts with 95% CI, (2) paired change in WER vs base with its CI and a vertical zero line, (3) Cardiff macro-F1 with CI; label fp17 '(registered)'; print changed-weight counts (and % of 37,760,640) and the long/short transcript counts as small text at the row ends; distinct fixed colors for base (gray), fp10 (orange) and fp17 (blue)

axes.x_left: word error rate vs human transcripts (test slice, n = 1,500)
axes.x_middle: change in word error rate vs base (paired bootstrap 95% CI)
axes.x_right: macro-F1 with the Cardiff sentiment model

caption: Weight-space edits to whisper-tiny (no training, 17 forward passes, 0.44% of weights rescaled). The registered checkpoint fp17 lowers the word error rate by 0.005 with a confidence interval that excludes zero, but lowers sentiment macro-F1 by 0.006, also significant. fp10 is a failed intermediate checkpoint kept for honesty.
